newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW - Holzmann sees liquidity easing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Holzmann sees liquidity easing.

text.p: German construction giant Philipp Holzmann AG sees its liquidity situation easing in the first quarter of 1997, a company official said on Friday.

Asia managing director Bob Kervorkian told Reuters the firm expected to book revenues early next year from sales of residential property, writedowns on which cost the company 448 million marks in 1995.
"It's going to be sold. We're expecting to raise 1.7 billion marks. With the liquidity requirements it has been decided to increase liquidity by selling certain assets," he said.
"I have to be careful but I've been told that liquidity will ease in January-February next year and negotiations are continuing with firm buyers."

Kervorkin said Holzmann's executive board had made a decision to focus more actively in fast expanding Asian markets after a slowdown in European growth, combined with the writedowns which lead Holzmann to report losses of 443 million marks for 1995.
"The executive board has made a conscious decision to move into Asia for the long term in a solid, committed way."
"I expect to see at least 10 percent of group revenues coming from South East Asia next year, up from around four to five percent at the moment," he added.

The company expected to generate core revenues from Thailand, estimated to contribute 10 billion baht ($395 million) next year following the recent signing of a 24-month, 2.3 billion baht bridge contract and a three-year, 22 billion baht deal for civil work on Bangkok's Hopewell project.

The Phillipines is expected to contribute six billion baht from a hospital construction and associated work, and Malaysia 2.5 billion baht from work on a shopping mall and cement plant though contracts have yet to be signed. The firm has generated no revenue from either country this year.

He said the company has tenders open on mass transit schemes in India including a mass transit systems in Bangalore and Dehli. Work this year has generated around 500 million baht, contracts signed are worth around five billion baht.
Kervorkian said margins on existing projects were currently between three to five percent.

In China, which reports directly to German headquarters, he said Holzmann had signed six contracts worth US$ 3 billion. They are the two hydro-power schemes, a Beijing shopping center, a Lufthansa center in Beijing, an Anheuser-Busch brewery, and a chemical plant construction for Bayer AG. ($ = 25.43 Thai Baht)
